correctness.rationale: Theorem 6 in arXiv:2307.05168 equates total visibility to avoidance of Hamming distance two. This leaves at most one selected even word and one odd word per third-cube layer. Across distinct layers the only forbidden opposite-parity pairs are three-bit distance one, forcing bit-complement labels. For fixed supports A,B the assignment count is 4^c of the complete bipartite index graph minus its equal-index diagonal. Exhaustive connectivity classification gives exactly the three correction types; the polynomial follows. Leading coefficients prove 2n maximum and n>=3 top-layer rigidity; n=2 is excluded correctly. A separate standalone enumeration for n=1..6 and direct geodesic BFS samples for n=1..3 passed.

originality.rationale: The 2023 Hamming paper proves the distance-two characterization and maxima for three factors, but gives only general bounds for four or more factors. The later open-access visibility-polynomial paper defines the enumeration invariant and universal inclusion-exclusion, not this infinite-family closed formula or rigidity. Available published findings on short-distance mutual visibility in ordinary hypercubes, and on three-factor lower total visibility, constrain different predicates or dimensions. Unindexed mixed-alphabet coding enumerations remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently termed code-theoretic enumerations for forbidden Hamming distance two on a mixed-alphabet Cartesian product could have equivalent coefficient formulas.
Literature inspection cannot establish absolute publication priority; independent review remains unperformed.

value.rationale: Determines the full cardinality polynomial, not merely a bound, for a canonical four-factor mixed-alphabet Hamming family directly motivated by the earlier three-factor classification. The exact threshold n+2 forces all larger total-visibility sets into one of four antipodal cylinders, identifying a sharp structural stability phenomenon; the polynomial also detects the Q4 exception and counts every cardinality. It gives an infinite family of nontrivial enumerations beyond the cited three-factor theorem.
